fullTitle.en: Track Earth & Environment: Climate Data and Services (300)
fullTitle.nl: Track Earth & Environment: Climate Data and Services (300)

description.en:
The course provides the students a glimpse into the key role that climate data and services play in climate change adaptation. 

Climate services bridge science and society for informed decision-making, providing climate data and information to support decisions makers and end-users. However, climate services must be based on traceable and quality-ensured climate data optimized for producing meaningful information for different users. Understanding the limitations and main uncertainty sources associated with climate data (generated by observations, satellite-derived data, and climate models) is critical to risk assessment and decision making.

Climate services are a crucial tool to take early action, reduce disaster risk for the foreseeable future, and support climate adaptation. Climate services include seasonal forecasts (e.g., forest fire outlook) and long-term projections (e.g., sea-level rise). Combined with societal indicators (e.g., population, income, and mobility), data provided by climate services are extremely important for assessing exposure and vulnerability and mitigating risks associated with climate extremes (i.e., heatwaves, droughts, wildfires, major storms, glacial lake outburst floods (GLOF), and harmful algal blooms (HABs)). These climate extremes pose a serious challenge to climate change adaptation, particularly in the Global South, where climate data and services are not available or are less reliable—for reasons we will also discuss in the course.  

The course will address the Sustainable Development Goals 13 (climate action) and 11 (sustainable communities). In particular, the student will learn how to use open, accessible, and downloadable, thoroughly described, machine-readable, and maintained over time data produced by well-known providers of climate services (e.g., NASA, NOAA, NSIDC, ESA, Copernicus, and KNMI). Climate data from these providers will be used to assess changes in the frequency and intensity of climate extremes. We will discuss how this information is essential for supporting smart decision making and climate adaptation efforts at local, regional, and global scales. 
 
By addressing several challenges related to climate change adaptation, this course connects to other courses (such as “Data for Future Energy and Climate”) that address various aspects of the climate change mitigation. Prior courses (such as “The Earth System”, and “Climate Change: Land, Earth and Water”) help to provide a theoretical basis for understanding the challenges to climate change adaptation posed by climate extremes. The course also relates to Systems for Integrated Knowledge Production, for the way it considers how scientific knowledge can connect to societal challenges and to decision-making.

assessmentsExplanation.en: The students will be assessed based on participation and other assessments. One of the assessments will be an individual project in which students will collect, organise, analyse and visualise a datasets, including the consideration of possible privacy and security concerns.
